examples: Many children in the refugee camp were severely undernourished.
بسیاری از کودکان در آن اردوگاه پناهجویان به شدت دچار سوءتغذیه بودند.
The vet said the stray cat looked undernourished and needed regular meals.
دامپزشک گفت آن گربه ولگرد دچار سوءتغذیه به نظر می‌رسد و به غذای منظم نیاز دارد.
Crops grown in poor soil often produce undernourished, weak plants.
محصولاتی که در خاک ضعیف کاشته می‌شوند، اغلب گیاهانی دچار سوءتغذیه و ضعیف تولید می‌کنند.
miniContext: Undernourished describes a person, animal, or even a plant that has not received enough food or nutrients to grow and function properly. Aid organizations often report alarming numbers of undernourished children in regions affected by famine or war. The word can also apply more broadly, such as undernourished soil failing to support healthy crops. In every case, being undernourished signals a serious and often visible lack of proper nutrition.

examples: The company refused to disclose how much money it had lost last year.
آن شرکت از فاش کردن اینکه سال گذشته چقدر پول از دست داده بود، خودداری کرد.
Witnesses must disclose everything they know, even if it is uncomfortable.
شاهدان باید هر چیزی که می‌دانند را فاش کنند، حتی اگر ناراحت‌کننده باشد.
She finally disclosed the truth about her illness to her closest friends.
او سرانجام حقیقت درباره بیماری‌اش را با نزدیک‌ترین دوستانش فاش کرد.
miniContext: To disclose information means to reveal it officially or deliberately, often information that was previously kept private or secret. Companies are legally required to disclose certain financial details to protect investors from being misled. On a personal level, someone might choose to disclose a difficult secret only to the people they trust most. The word carries a sense of formality, suggesting a deliberate decision to make something known rather than an accidental slip.

examples: The earthquake was the worst natural disaster the region had seen in decades.
آن زمین‌لرزه بدترین فاجعه طبیعی بود که آن منطقه در چند دهه گذشته به خود دیده بود.
Forgetting her passport turned the entire trip into a complete disaster.
فراموش کردن پاسپورتش آن سفر را کاملاً به یک فاجعه تبدیل کرد.
Emergency crews rushed to the scene of the disaster within minutes.
گروه‌های امداد در عرض چند دقیقه به محل آن فاجعه رسیدند.
miniContext: A disaster is an event causing widespread damage, suffering, or loss, whether from nature, accident, or human error. Earthquakes, floods, and fires are classic examples of natural disasters that governments must prepare to respond to quickly. The word is also used more loosely in everyday speech for anything that goes badly wrong, like a dinner party that turns into a disaster. Whether large-scale or personal, disaster always implies serious, often sudden, negative consequences.

examples: The outlaw hid in the mountains for years to avoid capture by the sheriff.
آن قانون‌شکن برای سال‌ها در کوه‌ها پنهان شد تا از دستگیری توسط کلانتر فرار کند.
Legends about the famous outlaw grew more exaggerated with each retelling.
افسانه‌ها درباره آن قانون‌شکن مشهور با هر بار بازگو شدن اغراق‌آمیزتر می‌شدند.
The sheriff organized a posse to track down the outlaw before nightfall.
کلانتر یک گروه تعقیب تشکیل داد تا قبل از فرا رسیدن شب، آن قانون‌شکن را ردیابی کند.
miniContext: An outlaw is someone who lives outside the law, often a criminal or bandit who actively evades capture by the authorities. In stories of the American Old West, the outlaw is a familiar figure, sometimes feared and sometimes romanticized as a rebel against unfair rule. Over time, tales about a famous outlaw often grow into legend, mixing real crimes with invented heroics. The word still carries a sense of defiance against official law and order.

examples: The restaurant charged an excessive fee just for sitting outside.
آن رستوران هزینه‌ای بیش از حد فقط برای نشستن در فضای بیرون دریافت کرد.
Doctors warned that excessive screen time was affecting the children's sleep.
پزشکان هشدار دادند که زمان بیش از حد استفاده از صفحه‌نمایش بر خواب کودکان اثر می‌گذارد.
His excessive drinking eventually cost him both his job and his marriage.
نوشیدن بیش از حد الکل سرانجام شغل و ازدواجش را از او گرفت.
miniContext: Excessive describes an amount or degree that goes beyond what is reasonable or necessary. An excessive fee feels unfair to customers, and excessive screen time worries parents concerned about their children's health. The word often appears as a warning, pointing out behavior or spending that has crossed a healthy limit. Whatever the context, excessive signals that something has gone too far.

examples: Police quickly identified the culprit behind the string of burglaries.
پلیس به سرعت مقصر پشت آن سری دزدی‌ها را شناسایی کرد.
After testing several theories, doctors found that stress was the real culprit behind her headaches.
پس از آزمودن چند فرضیه، پزشکان متوجه شدند که استرس مقصر اصلی سردردهای او بود.
Everyone in the office suspected the real culprit was the broken air conditioner, not the heat outside.
همه در اداره گمان می‌کردند مقصر اصلی، کولر خراب است، نه گرمای بیرون.
miniContext: A culprit is the person or thing responsible for a problem, crime, or unwanted result. Detectives work to identify the culprit behind a crime, while doctors sometimes search for the hidden culprit behind a mysterious illness. The word is also used lightly in everyday speech, like blaming a broken appliance as the culprit behind a frustrating afternoon. In every case, naming the culprit means pinpointing exactly what or who caused the trouble.

examples: The company decided to promote her to regional manager after only one year.
آن شرکت تصمیم گرفت پس از تنها یک سال، او را به مدیر منطقه‌ای ارتقا دهد.
The campaign aims to promote healthy eating among teenagers.
آن کمپین هدف دارد تغذیه سالم را در میان نوجوانان ترویج دهد.
Local businesses used social media to promote their new products.
کسب‌وکارهای محلی از شبکه‌های اجتماعی برای ترویج محصولات جدیدشان استفاده کردند.
miniContext: To promote someone means to raise them to a higher position, usually at work, while to promote an idea means to actively encourage and support it. Hardworking employees hope to promote within their company rather than start over somewhere new. Public health campaigns try to promote better habits, like healthy eating or regular exercise, through advertising and education. Businesses also promote their products constantly, competing for the attention of potential customers.

examples: The teacher used a simple diagram to illustrate how the heart pumps blood.
معلم از یک نمودار ساده استفاده کرد تا نشان دهد قلب چگونه خون را پمپاژ می‌کند.
This story perfectly illustrates why honesty matters, even when it's difficult.
این داستان به خوبی نشان می‌دهد که چرا صداقت مهم است، حتی وقتی سخت باشد.
The artist was hired to illustrate the children's book with colorful drawings.
آن هنرمند استخدام شد تا آن کتاب کودکان را با نقاشی‌های رنگارنگ تصویرسازی کند.
miniContext: To illustrate something means to make it clearer through an example, diagram, or image. Teachers often illustrate complex ideas with simple drawings so students can grasp them more easily. Writers also use illustrate in a more abstract sense, as when a specific story illustrates a broader point about human behavior. In publishing, an illustrator literally illustrates a book, adding pictures that bring the written words to life.

examples: She decided to insist on paying for dinner, even though it was his turn.
او تصمیم گرفت اصرار کند که هزینه شام را خودش بپردازد، حتی با اینکه نوبت او بود.
The doctor insisted that the patient rest for at least a week.
پزشک اصرار کرد که بیمار حداقل یک هفته استراحت کند.
No matter how many times he explained, she continued to insist she was right.
هر چند بار هم که او توضیح داد، او همچنان اصرار داشت که حق با خودش است.
miniContext: To insist means to demand something firmly, refusing to accept any alternative or change of plan. A generous friend might insist on paying the bill no matter how much you protest. Doctors sometimes insist on strict rest or treatment when a patient's health depends on following instructions carefully. The word conveys a strong, unwavering determination, often repeated until the other person gives in.

examples: The government tried to censor any news reports that criticized its policies.
دولت سعی کرد هر گزارش خبری‌ای را که سیاست‌هایش را نقد می‌کرد، سانسور کند.
The streaming platform decided to censor a few scenes before releasing the film.
آن پلتفرم پخش آنلاین تصمیم گرفت چند صحنه را قبل از انتشار آن فیلم سانسور کند.
Some parents choose to censor the content their children watch online.
برخی والدین ترجیح می‌دهند محتوایی را که فرزندانشان آنلاین تماشا می‌کنند، سانسور کنند.
miniContext: To censor something means to remove or restrict parts of it that are considered offensive, dangerous, or politically unacceptable. Governments sometimes censor news and media to control public opinion, which raises serious concerns about free speech. Film studios and streaming services may also censor certain scenes to meet rating requirements in different countries. On a smaller scale, parents often censor the media their children can access, trying to protect them from inappropriate content.

examples: The court sent the juvenile to a special rehabilitation program instead of adult prison.
دادگاه آن نوجوان را به یک برنامه بازپروری ویژه فرستاد، نه به زندان بزرگسالان.
As a juvenile, he was known for getting into minor trouble around the neighborhood.
در دوران نوجوانی، او به دردسر درست کردن‌های کوچک در اطراف محله معروف بود.
The zoo separates juveniles from adult animals to keep them safe.
آن باغ‌وحش حیوانات نوجوان را از حیوانات بالغ جدا نگه می‌دارد تا امن بمانند.
miniContext: A juvenile is a young person who has not yet reached full legal adulthood, often discussed in the context of behavior or the justice system. Courts handle juvenile offenders differently from adults, focusing more on rehabilitation than punishment. The word is also used in biology to describe young animals that have not yet reached maturity, such as juvenile birds still learning to fly. In every context, juvenile points to a stage of youth before full development.

examples: He attached a worm as bait to catch fish in the lake.
او یک کرم را به عنوان طعمه برای گرفتن ماهی در آن دریاچه وصل کرد.
The email promising free money was clearly bait for an online scam.
آن ایمیلی که پول رایگان وعده می‌داد، به‌وضوح طعمه‌ای برای یک کلاهبرداری آنلاین بود.
Hunters sometimes use bait to lure animals closer to a trap.
شکارچیان گاهی از طعمه برای نزدیک کردن حیوانات به یک تله استفاده می‌کنند.
miniContext: Bait is something used to attract and trap an animal, a fish, or even a person into a particular situation. Fishermen choose their bait carefully, knowing that different fish prefer different kinds of food. The word also applies to scams and traps, where a tempting offer serves as bait to lure unsuspecting victims. Whether literal or figurative, bait always works by appealing to desire before springing a trap.
